newsitem.title: UK: Transmitters pose no leukaemia risk, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Transmitters pose no leukaemia risk, study finds.

text.p: People living near radio or television transmitters do not have a higher risk of leukaemia, a study published by the British government on Tuesday found.
The Small Area Health Statistics Unit, a government-funded group, investigated how many cases of leukaemia there were near 20 high power television and FM radio transmitters across Britain.
It found no unusual numbers of cases among people living within two kilometres (1.2 miles) of the transmitters.

"These new data do not change our advice, given in 1994, that there is no firm evidence of a carcinogenic hazard from exposure to very low frequency electromagnetic fields, as far as this advice relates to TV and radio mast emissions," the government Committee on the Medical Aspects of Radiation in the Environment said.
